questions: With seven sensors, does the controller need its sensor_weights rescaled, or does the wider span make the signal saturate on tight bends?
Did line_loss_events fall to zero on slalom and s-bend, and did max_error stay under 0.060 m?
Does steering_oscillation rise with the wider array, which would suggest the outer sensors are reacting too early?
Is the mass of 0.6 kg still the right value, or does the current limit on completion time now come from speed rather than tracking?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If line loss is gone but oscillation rises, propose moving the forward sensor row toward y = 0.03 m. If max_error is still above 0.06 m with no line loss, the limit is turn authority rather than sensing, so propose a wider wheel_track.

intent: Widen the sensor array from ±0.024 m to ±0.036 m with seven contiguous 12 mm sensors, so the tape stays under a sensor at larger lateral offsets and line loss stops ending runs before the off-track limit. Keep the rest of the geometry fixed to isolate the sensing change. Expected result: line_loss_events drop toward zero on the slalom and s-bend, max_error falls below 0.060 m, and progress and completion improve on the oval and s-bend.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) line loss is the main cause of the off-track ends, so widening the span should lower line_loss_events and raise progress; (2) the off-track floor of 0.06 m cannot be raised by body width, so max_error must be held down by sensing and control; (3) the seven-sensor span will not raise steering oscillation sharply. Next race, check line_loss_events, max_error, progress and steering_oscillation per track against the iteration-0 baseline.
rationale: The race evidence is 60 trials with no finishes; every run ended off track. Max error on the oval was 0.0626 m, above the 0.060 m off-track floor, and line-loss events were 1 to 2 per run. Max error exceeds the limit, and the line is lost just before the robot leaves the track, so the failure is the sensor span, not tuning. The current span of ±0.024 m with 12 mm footprints loses the tape at roughly ±0.04 m offset, which is inside the drift the robot shows on the bends. Body width cannot help: the off-track limit stays at 0.06 m for any body width in range. Steering oscillation (0.13 to 0.25) is low, so the look-ahead is not the problem and I keep y = 0.04 m. I widen the array to seven sensors at 12 mm spacing with 12 mm footprints, spanning x = -0.036 to +0.036 m. The footprints stay contiguous, so the tape is always covered, and the line should hold to roughly ±0.054 m offset. This follows the Integrator's first contingency (widen the span when line loss is above zero) and goes slightly further than their suggested ±0.032 m to give the controller more margin on the tightest bends. Mass, wheel and body values are unchanged so that the effect of the sensor change can be read cleanly. Expected result: line_loss_events near zero on slalom and s-bend, max_error below 0.06 m, and progress rising on all three tracks.
